title: ～がり — a person who easily feels ～
summary: がり is a suffix attached to the stem of an adjective to make a noun meaning ‘a person who tends to feel ～’. 寒がり means someone who easily feels cold. It describes a person's tendency or character.

patterns.gloss: adjective stem + がり (寒い → 寒がり, 暑い → 暑がり)
na-adjective stem + がり (怖い・さびしがり)

body.p: Drop い from an い-adjective and add がり: 寒い → 寒がり, 暑い → 暑がり, 恥ずかしい → 恥ずかしがり (shy), 怖い → 怖がり (easily scared). A few な-adjectives also work, like さびしがり.
It names a type of person by their usual tendency: 妹は寒がりです (my sister feels the cold easily). It is a noun, so it can take です, の and other particles.
がり comes from the verb ～がる (to show signs of feeling ～), which is used to describe other people's feelings: 寒がっている. The noun がり turns that into a trait.

examples.ja: 妹（いもうと）は寒（さむ）がりです。
examples.tr: My sister is sensitive to the cold.

examples.ja: 父（ちち）は暑（あつ）がりで、冬（ふゆ）でも窓（まど）を開（あ）ける。
examples.romaji: Chichi wa atsugari de, fuyu demo mado o akeru.
examples.tr: My father tends to feel hot easily, and opens the window even in winter.
examples.note: 暑がりで links to the next clause.

examples.ja: その子（こ）は恥（は）ずかしがりで、あまり話（はな）さない。
examples.romaji: Sono ko wa hazukashigari de, amari hanasanai.
examples.tr: That child is shy and doesn't talk much.
examples.note: 恥ずかしい → 恥ずかし + がり.

pitfalls: Drop い before がり: 寒がり, not 寒いがり.
がり describes a general tendency of a person, not a feeling at this moment. For the moment, use ～がる (寒がっている).
